title_en: Regulations on the Implementation of the Government Procurement Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Government Procurement Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Government Procurement Law).

Article 2 Fiscal funds as mentioned in Article 2 of the Government Procurement Law means funds included in budget management.
Borrowed funds with fiscal funds as repayment source shall be deemed as fiscal funds.
Where a procurement project of a state organ, public institution or social organization uses both fiscal funds and non-fiscal funds, the part purchased with fiscal funds shall be governed by the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations; where fiscal funds and non-fiscal funds cannot be separately purchased, the whole procurement shall be uniformly governed by the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations.
Services as mentioned in Article 2 of the Government Procurement Law include services needed by the government itself and public services provided by the government to the public.

Article 3 The centralized procurement catalogue includes items procured by centralized procurement agencies and items procured by department centralized procurement.
Items with unified technical and service standards and commonly used by procuring entities shall be classified as items procured by centralized procurement agencies; items for which a procuring entity's own department or system has special requirements based on business needs and which may be procured uniformly shall be classified as items procured by department centralized procurement.

Article 4 Centralized procurement as mentioned in the Government Procurement Law means the act of a procuring entity entrusting a centralized procurement agency to procure on its behalf items listed in the centralized procurement catalogue, or conducting department centralized procurement; decentralized procurement as mentioned therein means the act of a procuring entity purchasing on its own or entrusting a procurement agency to purchase on its behalf items that are above the procurement threshold and not listed in the centralized procurement catalogue.

Article 5 The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government, or agencies authorized by them, may, in light of actual circumstances, determine the centralized procurement catalogues and procurement thresholds respectively applicable at the provincial, city-with-districts and county levels within their administrative regions.

Article 6 The finance department of the State Council shall, in accordance with the national economic and social development policies and in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, formulate government procurement policies. Through measures such as formulating procurement demand standards, reserving procurement shares, offering price evaluation preferences, and giving priority to procurement, it shall achieve objectives including energy conservation, environmental protection, supporting underdeveloped areas and ethnic minority regions, and promoting the development of small and medium-sized enterprises.

Article 7 Where a government procurement project of construction works, or goods or services related to construction works, is procured by way of tendering, the Bidding and Tendering Law of the People's Republic of China and its implementing regulations shall apply; where it is procured by other means, the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations shall apply.
Construction works as mentioned in the preceding paragraph means construction projects, including the construction, reconstruction, expansion of buildings and structures and the related decoration, demolition, repair, etc.; goods related to construction works means equipment, materials, etc. that form an integral part of the works and are necessary for realizing the basic functions of the works; services related to construction works means services such as survey, design, and supervision required for completing the works.
Government procurement of construction works and goods or services related to construction works shall implement government procurement policies.

Article 8 Information on government procurement projects shall be published on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level. Where the budget amount of a procurement project reaches the standard prescribed by the finance department of the State Council, the information on the government procurement project shall be published on the media designated by the finance department of the State Council.

Article 10 The State shall implement unified construction standards for electronic trading platforms for government procurement, and promote the use of information networks for electronic government procurement activities.

Article 11 In government procurement activities, the procuring entity shall safeguard the national interest and the public interest, be impartial and honest, act in good faith, implement government procurement policies, establish internal management systems for government procurement, practice strict economy, and determine procurement needs in a scientific and reasonable manner.
A procuring entity shall not demand or accept gifts, kickbacks, or other goods or services unrelated to the procurement from suppliers.

Article 12 Procurement agencies as mentioned in the Government Procurement Law mean centralized procurement agencies and procurement agencies other than centralized procurement agencies.
A centralized procurement agency is a non-profit public institution legally established by the people's government at or above the city with districts level, and is an executing agency for acting as agent for centralized procurement projects. A centralized procurement agency shall, based on the entrustment of the procuring entity, formulate implementation plans for centralized procurement projects, specify procurement procedures, and organize government procurement activities; it shall not subcontract centralized procurement projects. Procurement agencies other than centralized procurement agencies are social intermediary organizations engaged in procurement agency business.

Article 13 A procurement agency shall establish a sound internal supervision and management system for government procurement, and possess the evaluation conditions and facilities necessary for conducting government procurement business.
A procurement agency shall improve its professional service level in determining procurement needs, preparing tender documents, negotiation documents, and request for quotation notices, drafting contract texts, and optimizing procurement procedures; promptly organize, within the prescribed time limit based on the entrustment of the procuring entity, the signing of a government procurement contract between the procuring entity and the winning or successful supplier; and promptly assist the procuring entity in carrying out acceptance inspection of the procurement project.

Article 14 A procurement agency shall not obtain government procurement agency business by improper means, and shall not collude maliciously with the procuring entity or suppliers to manipulate government procurement activities.
Staff members of a procurement agency shall not accept banquets, tours, or entertainment organized by the procuring entity or suppliers; shall not accept gifts, cash, negotiable securities, etc.; and shall not have expenses that should be borne personally reimbursed by the procuring entity or suppliers.

Article 15 The procuring entity and the procurement agency shall prepare procurement documents in accordance with government procurement policies, procurement budgets, and procurement needs.
Procurement needs shall comply with the technical, service, safety and other requirements prescribed by laws, regulations and government procurement policies. For public service projects provided by the government to the public, opinions of the public shall be solicited in determining procurement needs. Unless it is impossible to determine detailed specifications or specific requirements due to technical complexity or special nature, procurement needs shall be complete and clear. When necessary, opinions of relevant suppliers and experts shall be solicited in determining procurement needs.

Article 16 The entrustment agency agreement as prescribed in Article 20 of the Government Procurement Law shall specify specific matters such as the scope, authority and term of the agency procurement.
The procuring entity and the procurement agency shall perform their respective obligations in accordance with the entrustment agency agreement, and the procurement agency shall not exceed the scope of its agency authority.

Article 18 Different suppliers whose persons in charge of the entity are the same person or which have a relationship of direct holding or management shall not participate in the same government procurement activity under the same contract.
Except for single-source procurement projects, a supplier that has provided services such as overall design, specification preparation, project management, supervision, or inspection for a procurement project shall not participate in any other procurement activities of that procurement project.

Article 19 Major illegal record as mentioned in Item (5) of Paragraph 1 of Article 22 of the Government Procurement Law means that the supplier has been subject to criminal punishment or administrative penalties including order to suspend production or business, revocation of permit or license, or relatively large amount of fine due to illegal business operations.
Where a supplier has been prohibited from participating in government procurement activities for a certain period within the 3 years prior to participating in a government procurement activity due to illegal business operations, it may participate in government procurement activities after the expiry of such period.

Article 21 Where a procuring entity or procurement agency conducts a prequalification of suppliers, the announcement of prequalification shall be published on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level. Where prequalification has been carried out, the eligibility of suppliers may no longer be examined during the evaluation stage. If the eligibility of a prequalified supplier changes during the evaluation stage, it shall notify the procuring entity and the procurement agency.
The prequalification announcement shall include the names of the procuring entity and the procurement project, procurement needs, qualification requirements for suppliers, and the time and place for suppliers to submit their prequalification application documents. The time for submitting prequalification application documents shall be no less than 5 working days from the date of publication of the announcement.

Article 22 Where suppliers with the same type of qualification in a consortium undertake the same work according to the division of labor in the consortium, the qualification level shall be determined in accordance with the supplier having the lower qualification level.
Where a consortium participates in a government procurement activity, the parties to the consortium shall not separately participate in, or form another consortium with other suppliers to participate in, the same government procurement activity under the same contract.

Article 23 Where a procuring entity procures goods or services above the threshold for public tendering, and the circumstances specified in Article 29, 30, 31 or 32 of the Government Procurement Law are met, or there are special circumstances such as the need to implement government procurement policies, the procuring entity may, upon approval by the finance department of the people's government at or above the city with districts level, adopt procurement methods other than public tendering in accordance with law.

Article 24 For items listed in the centralized procurement catalogue that are suitable for bulk centralized procurement, bulk centralized procurement shall be implemented, except for emergency small-value sporadic goods projects and service or construction projects with special requirements.

Article 25 Where a government procurement project of construction works is not subject to tendering according to law, it shall be procured by way of competitive negotiation or single-source procurement as prescribed in the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations.

Article 26 The circumstances specified in Item (3) of Article 30 of the Government Procurement Law shall be those unforeseen by the procuring entity or not caused by the procuring entity's delay; the circumstances specified in Item (4) mean that the total price cannot be calculated in advance due to the procurement of artworks, patents, proprietary technologies, or because the time or quantity of services cannot be determined in advance, etc.

Article 27 The circumstances specified in Item (1) of Article 31 of the Government Procurement Law mean that, due to the use of irreplaceable patents or proprietary technologies in the goods or services, or due to special requirements of a public service project, the procurement can only be made from a particular supplier.

Article 28 Within a fiscal year, where a procuring entity conducts multiple procurements of goods or services under the same budget item and of the same heading or category by means other than public tendering, and the cumulative amount exceeds the threshold for public tendering, this constitutes circumvention of public tendering by breaking down the procurement into smaller parts, unless the project budget has been adjusted or the procurement by means other than public tendering has been approved.

Article 29 A procuring entity shall, based on the centralized procurement catalogue, procurement thresholds and the approved departmental budget, formulate a government procurement implementation plan and submit it to the finance department of the people's government at the same level for record.
Article 30 The procuring entity or procurement agency shall disclose the budget amount of the procurement project in the tender documents, negotiation documents, and request for quotation notices.

Article 31 The period for providing tender documents shall be no less than 5 working days from the date on which the tender documents begin to be issued.
The procuring entity or procurement agency may make necessary clarifications or modifications to the issued tender documents. If the content of the clarification or modification may affect the preparation of bid documents, the procuring entity or procurement agency shall notify in writing all potential bidders who have obtained the tender documents at least 15 days before the deadline for submission of bids; if less than 15 days remain, the procuring entity or procurement agency shall extend the deadline for submission of bid documents.

Article 32 The procuring entity or procurement agency shall prepare the tender documents in accordance with the standard text of tender documents formulated by the finance department of the State Council.
The tender documents shall include the commercial conditions of the procurement project, procurement needs, qualification conditions of bidders, requirements for bid price, evaluation methods, evaluation criteria, and the proposed contract text, etc.

Article 33 Where the tender documents require bidders to submit bid bonds, the bid bond shall not exceed 2% of the budget amount of the procurement project. The bid bond shall be submitted in non-cash forms such as checks, drafts, promissory notes, or letters of guarantee issued by financial institutions or guarantee institutions. If a bidder fails to submit a bid bond as required by the tender documents, its bid shall be invalid.
The procuring entity or procurement agency shall, within 5 working days from the date of issuance of the notice of award, return the bid bonds to the unsuccessful bidders, and within 5 working days from the date of signing of the government procurement contract, return the bid bond to the winning bidder.
Where a supplier participating in competitive negotiation or quotation procurement is required to submit a bond, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall be applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 34 The bid evaluation methods for government procurement tendering are divided into the lowest evaluated bid price method and the comprehensive score method.
The lowest evaluated bid price method means an evaluation method whereby the supplier whose bid document meets all substantive requirements of the tender documents and whose evaluated bid price is the lowest is selected as the candidate for winning the bid. The comprehensive score method means an evaluation method whereby the supplier whose bid document meets all substantive requirements of the tender documents and whose evaluation score based on quantified indicators of evaluation factors is the highest is selected as the candidate for winning the bid.
For goods and service projects with unified technical, service and other standards, the lowest evaluated bid price method shall be adopted.
Where the comprehensive score method is adopted, the score allocation in the evaluation criteria shall correspond to the quantified indicators of the evaluation factors.
Evaluation criteria not specified in the tender documents shall not be used as the basis for evaluation.

Article 35 Where the negotiation documents cannot completely and clearly specify the procurement needs and the suppliers are required to provide final design plans or solutions, after the negotiation concludes, the negotiation team shall, in accordance with the principle of majority rule, vote to recommend the design plans or solutions of 3 or more suppliers, and require them to submit final quotations within a prescribed time.

Article 36 The request for quotation notice shall determine the terms of the government procurement contract based on the procurement needs. During the quotation process, the quotation team shall not alter the terms of the government procurement contract as determined in the request for quotation notice.

Article 37 The term "equal quality and services" as mentioned in Item (5) of Article 38 and Item (4) of Article 40 of the Government Procurement Law means that the product quality and services provided by the supplier both satisfy the substantive requirements prescribed in the procurement documents.

Article 38 Where a procurement reaches the threshold for public tendering, meets the circumstances specified in Item (1) of Article 31 of the Government Procurement Law, and can only be procured from the sole supplier, the procuring entity shall publicize the procurement project information and the name of the sole supplier on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level, with a publicity period of no less than 5 working days.

Article 39 Except for circumstances prescribed by the finance department of the State Council, the procuring entity or procurement agency shall randomly select evaluation experts from the government procurement evaluation expert database.

Article 40 Government procurement evaluation experts shall observe the discipline of evaluation work, and shall not disclose evaluation documents, evaluation status, or trade secrets learned during evaluation.
Where the bid evaluation committee, competitive negotiation team, or quotation team discovers during the evaluation process that a supplier has engaged in illegal acts such as bribery, providing false materials, or collusion, it shall promptly report to the finance department.
Where a government procurement evaluation expert is subject to illegal interference during the evaluation process, he or she shall promptly report to the finance, supervision or other departments.

Article 41 Members of the bid evaluation committee, competitive negotiation team, or quotation team shall conduct independent evaluation in accordance with the principles of objectivity, fairness and prudence, and based on the evaluation procedures, evaluation methods and evaluation criteria specified in the procurement documents. If the content of the procurement documents violates the relevant mandatory provisions of the State, the bid evaluation committee, competitive negotiation team or quotation team shall suspend the evaluation and explain the situation to the procuring entity or procurement agency.
Members of the bid evaluation committee, competitive negotiation team, or quotation team shall sign the evaluation report and bear legal liability for their own evaluation opinions. If a member dissents from the evaluation report, he or she shall sign the evaluation report indicating the dissent and stating the reasons; otherwise, he or she shall be deemed to have agreed to the evaluation report.

Article 42 The procuring entity or procurement agency shall not make any tendentious or misleading explanations or statements to the evaluation experts of the bid evaluation committee, competitive negotiation team, or quotation team.

Article 43 The procurement agency shall, within 2 working days from the date of conclusion of the evaluation, deliver the evaluation report to the procuring entity. The procuring entity shall, within 5 working days from the date of receipt of the evaluation report, determine the winning or successful supplier in order from among the candidates for winning the bid or concluding the transaction recommended in the evaluation report.
The procuring entity or procurement agency shall, within 2 working days from the date of determination of the winning or successful supplier, issue the notice of award or notice of successful transaction, and announce the result of the winning bid or successful transaction on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level; the tender documents, competitive negotiation documents, and request for quotation notices shall be announced simultaneously with the result of the winning bid or successful transaction.
The content of the announcement of the result of the winning bid or successful transaction shall include the names, addresses and contact details of the procuring entity and procurement agency, the project name and project number, the name and address of the winning or successful supplier and the winning or successful amount, the names, specifications, quantities, unit prices, service requirements of the main winning or successful subject matter, and the list of evaluation experts.

Article 44 Except for circumstances prescribed by the finance department of the State Council, the procuring entity or procurement agency shall not organize a re-evaluation for any reason. Where the procuring entity or procurement agency organizes a re-evaluation in accordance with the provisions of the finance department of the State Council, it shall submit a written report to the finance department of the people's government at the same level.
The procuring entity or procurement agency shall not alter the evaluation results by means such as testing samples or inspecting suppliers.

Article 45 The procuring entity or procurement agency shall, in accordance with the technical, service and safety standards specified in the government procurement contract, organize the acceptance inspection of the supplier's performance and issue an acceptance certificate. The acceptance certificate shall include the performance of each technical, service and safety standard.
For public service projects provided by the government to the public, service recipients shall be invited to participate and provide opinions during the acceptance inspection, and the acceptance results shall be announced to the public.
Article 46 The procurement documents as prescribed in Article 42 of the Government Procurement Law may be preserved in the form of electronic archives.
Article 47 The finance department of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, formulate standard texts for government procurement contracts.

Article 48 Where the procurement documents require the winning or successful supplier to submit a performance bond, the supplier shall submit it in non-cash forms such as checks, drafts, promissory notes, or letters of guarantee issued by financial institutions or guarantee institutions. The amount of the performance bond shall not exceed 10% of the amount of the government procurement contract.

Article 49 Where the winning or successful supplier refuses to sign a contract with the procuring entity, the procuring entity may, in accordance with the order of the list of candidates for winning the bid or concluding the transaction recommended in the evaluation report, determine the next candidate as the winning or successful supplier, or may restart the government procurement activity.

Article 50 The procuring entity shall, within 2 working days from the date of signing the government procurement contract, announce the government procurement contract on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level, except for the content involving State secrets or trade secrets in the government procurement contract.

Article 51 The procuring entity shall, in accordance with the provisions of the government procurement contract, promptly pay the procurement funds to the winning or successful supplier.
The payment procedure for funds of a government procurement project shall be executed in accordance with the State's provisions on the management of fiscal fund payments.

Article 52 The procuring entity or procurement agency shall, within 3 working days, respond to an inquiry raised by a supplier in accordance with law.
Where an inquiry or challenge raised by a supplier exceeds the scope of authority entrusted by the procuring entity to the procurement agency, the procurement agency shall inform the supplier to raise the matter with the procuring entity.
Government procurement evaluation experts shall cooperate with the procuring entity or procurement agency in responding to suppliers' inquiries and challenges.

Article 54 Where an inquiry or challenge may affect the result of winning the bid or concluding the transaction, the procuring entity shall suspend the signing of the contract; if the contract has already been signed, it shall suspend the performance of the contract.

Article 55 A supplier's challenge or complaint shall have clear claims and necessary supporting materials. The matters on which a supplier files a complaint shall not exceed the scope of the matters already challenged.

Article 56 The finance department shall handle complaint matters by way of written review, and may, when necessary, conduct investigation and evidence collection or organize cross-examination.
With respect to investigation and evidence collection conducted by the finance department in accordance with law, the complainant and the parties concerned with the complaint matters shall truthfully reflect the circumstances and provide relevant materials.

Article 57 Where a complainant fabricates facts, provides false materials, or obtains evidentiary materials by illegal means to file a complaint, the finance department shall dismiss the complaint.
After the finance department accepts a complaint, if the complainant applies in writing to withdraw the complaint, the finance department shall terminate the complaint processing procedure.

Article 58 Where the finance department needs to conduct inspection, testing, expert evaluation, or requires the complainant to supplement materials when handling a complaint matter, the time required shall not be counted in the complaint processing period.
The decision made by the finance department on the complaint matter shall be announced on the media designated by the finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level.

Article 59 The procurement standards for government procurement projects as mentioned in Article 63 of the Government Procurement Law mean the budget standards, asset allocation standards, technical and service standards, etc., on which the project procurement is based.

Article 61 Where a procuring entity discovers that a procurement agency has engaged in illegal acts, it shall require the procurement agency to correct them. If the procurement agency refuses to correct them, the procuring entity shall report to the finance department of the people's government at the same level, and the finance department shall handle the matter in accordance with law.
Where a procurement agency discovers that the procurement needs of a procuring entity contain differential treatment or discriminatory treatment against suppliers based on unreasonable conditions, or other content that does not conform to laws, regulations, or government procurement policies, or discovers that the procuring entity has other illegal acts, it shall advise the procuring entity to correct them. If the procuring entity refuses to correct them, the procurement agency shall report to the finance department of the people's government at the same level as the procuring entity, and the finance department shall handle the matter in accordance with law.

Article 62 The finance departments of the people's governments at or above the provincial level shall implement dynamic management of the government procurement evaluation expert database, and the specific management measures shall be formulated by the finance department of the State Council.
The procuring entity or procurement agency shall record the performance of duties by evaluation experts in government procurement activities, and promptly report to the finance department.

Article 63 The finance departments and other relevant departments of the people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the supervision and management of suppliers, procurement agencies, and evaluation experts participating in government procurement activities, record their不良 conduct, and incorporate such records into a unified credit information platform.

Article 64 The finance departments of the people's governments at all levels, when conducting supervision and inspection over government procurement activities, have the power to consult and copy relevant documents and materials, and the relevant units and persons shall cooperate.

Article 65 The audit authorities, supervision authorities, and other relevant departments shall, in accordance with law, supervise government procurement activities, and if they discover that a procurement party has engaged in illegal acts, they shall promptly notify the finance department.

Article 66 The fine prescribed in Article 71 of the Government Procurement Law shall be an amount of not more than 100,000 yuan.
The fine prescribed in Article 72 of the Government Procurement Law shall be an amount of not less than 50,000 yuan and not more than 250,000 yuan.

Article 70 Where a procurement person has an interest with a supplier but fails to withdraw in accordance with law, the finance department shall give him or her a warning and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan and not more than 20,000 yuan.

Article 71 Where any of the illegal acts specified in Article 71 or 72 of the Government Procurement Law has occurred and affects or may affect the result of winning the bid or concluding the transaction, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the following provisions:
(1) If the winning or successful supplier has not yet been determined, terminate this government procurement activity and restart a new government procurement activity.
(2) If the winning or successful supplier has been determined but the government procurement contract has not yet been signed, the result of winning the bid or successful transaction shall be void, and a new winning or successful supplier shall be determined from among the qualified candidates for winning the bid or concluding the transaction; if there is no qualified candidate, restart the government procurement activity.
(3) If the government procurement contract has been signed but not yet performed, revoke the contract, and determine a new winning or successful supplier from among the qualified candidates for winning the bid or concluding the transaction; if there is no qualified candidate, restart the government procurement activity.
(4) If the government procurement contract has been performed, causing losses to the procuring entity or supplier, the responsible person shall bear compensation liability.
Where a government procurement party has other acts violating the Government Procurement Law or these Regulations, and after correction, such acts still affect or may affect the result of winning the bid or concluding the transaction, or are determined to render the winning bid or successful transaction void according to law, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 73 Where a supplier fabricates facts, provides false materials, or obtains evidentiary materials by illegal means to file a complaint, the finance department shall include it in the list of records of不良 conduct and prohibit it from participating in government procurement activities for 1 to 3 years.

Article 75 Where a government procurement evaluation expert fails to conduct independent evaluation in accordance with the evaluation procedures, evaluation methods and evaluation criteria specified in the procurement documents, or discloses evaluation documents or evaluation status, the finance department shall give him or her a warning and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan and not more than 20,000 yuan; if the result of winning the bid or concluding the transaction is affected, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed, and he or she shall be prohibited from participating in government procurement evaluation activities.
Where a government procurement evaluation expert has an interest with a supplier and fails to withdraw, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed, and he or she shall be prohibited from participating in government procurement evaluation activities.
Where a government procurement evaluation expert accepts bribes from the procuring entity, procurement agency, or supplier, or obtains other improper benefits, if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law; if it does not yet constitute a crime, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed, and he or she shall be prohibited from participating in government procurement evaluation activities.
Where a government procurement evaluation expert has any of the above illegal acts, his or her evaluation opinions shall be void, and he or she shall not obtain evaluation fees; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; if losses are caused to others, civil liability shall be borne in accordance with law.
Article 76 A government procurement party that violates the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations and causes losses to others shall bear civil liability in accordance with law.

Article 77 Where the finance department, in performing its duty of supervision and administration over government procurement, violates the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations by abusing its power, neglecting its duty, or engaging in malpractice for personal gain, the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions in accordance with law; if the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 78 A county people's government whose fiscal management is under the direct administration of the province may, as needed and upon approval by the provincial people's government, exercise the powers of the people's government at the city with districts level to approve changes to procurement methods as prescribed in the Government Procurement Law and these Regulations.
Article 79 These Regulations shall come into force as of March 1, 2015.
